thread:
Maya: Quick sync — we received two tickets where customers uploaded legacy .bin checkpoints and our warmup path fails with hard errors. They can't regenerate sharded safetensors easily. Need a low-friction migration approach.
Chris: What exact failures? header parse? bad offsets?
Maya: Stack shows index lookup failing and CRC mismatch during full manifest validation while hotstarting. Our index-first path rejects files.
Samuel: Idea: a compatibility shim that exposes an index-on-read abstraction. Lazily generate a manifest stub while streaming ranges, validate in background.
Lee: I prototyped: bin->stub manifest that (1) streams byte ranges, (2) emits per-chunk rolling checksums, (3) builds an ephemeral index cached in object storage. Background validator upgrades or flags corrupt shards.
Chris: Sounds workable. Two concerns: (A) don't OOM when streaming; (B) don't persist unverified manifests that could be abused.
Zara: Proposal: "gentle-migrate" mode behind a feature flag. Shim creates ephemeral signed manifest stubs with per-shard checksums computed incrementally. Stubs are marked unverified in Console until explicit promote.
Maya: Host rollout wise we should enable read-only shim first. No auto-promotion for hosted customers. Dedicated/private get opt-in migration tooling.
Samuel: Implementation bullets: streaming reader must bound memory (never > 2x chunk_size), compute rolling CRC per chunk, persist stub manifest with timestamps and partial checksums, schedule background full-validate job per-shard.
Lee: Add loader API: load.checkpoint_compat({ path, mode: "gentle" }) -> { manifest_ref, verified: bool } — manifest_ref must be internal ID or signed URL with ACL.
Chris: Example config we can expose to customers/operators: 
```json
{ "compat_mode": "gentle", "lazy_verify": true, "background_validate": true, "index_policy": "ephemeral-then-promote" }
```
Maya: How do we handle provenance/signing? We can't treat shim-created manifests as authoritative.
Samuel: Shim manifests are unsigned by default and flagged "unverified-origin" in the audit stream. Promotion requires running full-validate which produces a signed manifest using the ingest signing flow (KMS/HSM).
Chris: Edge-case: overlapping ranges / structural corruption. Detect overlaps during streaming and fail-fast for that shard. Only soft failures (checksum mismatch) go to background-validation.
Lee: Also ensure the background validator can mark a shard as degraded and the smart router will route requests to fallback model variants rather than serving bad tokens.
Zara: Rollout checklist (high level): infra: compat flag in loader service; eng-ml: streaming stub + background validator; devex: CLI rw-binshim with convert/promote; support: KB + examples; SRE: alerts for validation-fail spikes.
Chris: CLI examples for operators: 
./rw-binshim convert --input model-v1.bin --index-only --out s3://bucket/tmp-stub  # creates ephemeral stub
./rw-binshim promote --stub s3://bucket/tmp-stub --sign-with kms://proj/key  # runs full-validate and signs manifest
Maya: Metrics to add: compat.stub_created, compat.promoted, compat.validation_fail, compat.degraded_shard_count, and histograms for background-validate latency.
Samuel: Security note: manifest_ref must not be a raw S3 path without ACL checks. Use internal IDs or signed URLs that expire and check namespace/customer permissions.
Chris: Feature toggle should be per-namespace so we can test on a few enterprise customers first. No global default ON.
dev-bot: RFC follow-up PR opened -> https://git.redwood/eng-ml/rfcs/### (draft)
deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC -> 1% hosted traffic
Maya: I'll own loader implementation. Samuel owns background validator. Chris+Lee will pair on manifest format + loader ABI. Zara will run rollout + docs + KB.
Zara: I'll draft release notes and a support playbook after we have e2e tests passing.
Maya: Thanks everyone, will post PR link once branch exists. :thumbsup:
